name: Run the dam safety program (one dam safety task)
summary: As owner of about two dozen dams, dikes and canals behind its seventeen hydro plants, the company must keep each dam's consequence classification, operation and surveillance manual and emergency plan current, inspect the dams, analyse instrument readings, track deficiencies, commission periodic dam safety reviews from qualified consultants and report to the provincial dam safety regulator. A small team of dam safety engineers does this with help from the area operator-maintainers, and the area manager and director review what goes to the regulator. Tasks are slow because inspections depend on season, reservoir level and site access, reports queue behind other work, emergency plan exercises depend on municipalities' calendars, and dam safety reviews take months with consultants.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with seventeen hydro plants on the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman rivers run from one Calgary control centre, alongside converted gas units and wind farms.
baseline.notes: Task tracker and deficiency register in spreadsheets, documents in a document store, instrument data in the historian, submissions by portal or email, as in 2019-2022.

trigger: A task falls due on the dam safety compliance calendar, or site staff report a condition at a dam.
end_state: The task's report is filed internally, or it has been submitted to and accepted by the regulator, with any maintenance work requested.

volume.seasonality: Inspections cluster from June to October when sites are free of snow; instrument reviews and manual updates spread through the year.

evidence.note: About 25 dam structures: about 25 annual inspections, 40 to 60 instrument reviews, 10 manual or plan updates, 3 dam safety reviews and 10 to 20 follow-ups a year give about 8 tasks a month. Structure count is an estimate from the 17 plants in s6.

surge.cause: special inspections and follow-up after a flood or high-flow event

evidence.note: Estimate; special inspections are expected after floods.
Most of the four engineers' time; the rest goes to flood operations, capital projects and licence work.
Report reviews; estimate.

resources.name: Hydro plant with dam and reservoir

steps.name: Open dam safety task
steps.description: A dam safety engineer opens the next task from the dam safety compliance calendar (annual inspection, instrumentation review, manual or emergency plan review, dam safety review) or from a condition reported by site staff, and logs it in the task tracker with the dam, the due date and the requirement it meets.

error.defect_description: Due date or requirement recorded wrongly.

evidence.note: Owner duties to assess, review and report periodically (s1, s2); queue time estimated.

steps.name: Gather records for the dam
steps.description: The engineer pulls the dam's consequence classification, last inspection and dam safety review reports, open deficiencies, drawings, the operation, maintenance and surveillance manual and the instrumentation data from the historian.

error.defect_description: An older drawing or superseded manual is used.

evidence.note: Task types from owner duties (s1) and comparable frequencies (s8): about 25 dams with annual inspections, quarterly to annual instrument reviews, 7 to 10 year manual and review cycles. Mix is an estimate.

steps.name: Arrange site inspection
steps.description: The engineer books a date with the area operator-maintainers, picks a time when reservoir level and weather expose the features to be seen, and arranges boat or ice access and any gate tests with the control centre.

evidence.note: Most inspections are done in summer and autumn when sites are clear of snow; wait estimated.

steps.name: Travel to dam
steps.description: The engineer drives from Calgary to the dam, up to three hours each way for the North Saskatchewan plants, and meets the operator-maintainer at site.

evidence.note: Plant locations (s6); drive times estimated.

steps.name: Inspect dam structures
steps.description: The engineer walks the crest, faces, abutments, spillway, outlet works and toe, compares cracks, seepage, settlement and erosion with the last report, photographs changes and notes deficiencies on the checklist.

error.defect_description: A developing seepage or crack is missed.

control.basis: Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive: surveillance and periodic assessment by qualified professionals

evidence.note: Periodic assessments by qualified professionals (s1); annual formal inspections in comparable regulation (s8).

steps.name: Test-operate gates and outlets
steps.description: While the engineer inspects, the operator-maintainer runs each spillway gate, low-level outlet and backup power supply through its test, with the control centre watching levels, and records opening times and any binding or alarms.

control.basis: OMS manual under the Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive (annual test operation of gates and outlets, as in BC Dam Safety Regulation Schedule 2)

evidence.note: Annual test operation of spillway gates, outlets and equipment in comparable regulation (s8).

steps.name: Analyse instrumentation readings
steps.description: The engineer plots piezometer levels, seepage weir flows, survey monument movement and inclinometer readings against reservoir level and alarm thresholds, and looks for trends that differ from past years.

error.defect_description: A trend is masked by a faulty instrument.

evidence.note: Instrument readings collected and interpreted at least annually (s8); continuous monitoring duty (s9).

steps.name: Assess condition and deficiencies
steps.description: The engineer judges the dam's condition from the inspection, gate tests and instrument trends, rates each deficiency by its safety effect, and decides whether any finding is a hazardous condition that must go to the regulator now.

error.defect_description: A deficiency is rated too low.

evidence.note: Share of tasks finding a hazardous condition estimated.

steps.name: Report hazardous condition to regulator
steps.description: The engineer phones and then writes to the provincial dam safety regulator describing the condition, the actions taken (lower the reservoir, increase surveillance) and next steps, after informing the area manager and director.

control.basis: Water (Ministerial) Regulation Part 6: report hazardous conditions to the Director

evidence.note: Reporting duty from s1; times estimated.

steps.name: Update deficiency register
steps.description: The engineer enters new and closed deficiencies in the register with rating, owner and target date, and decides which need maintenance work and which need engineering study or capital.

error.defect_description: Closed item not closed or duplicate entry.

control.basis: Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive: owners track and address deficiencies and report them

evidence.note: Deficiency tracking and reporting (s1, s2); share needing work estimated.

steps.name: Raise maintenance work request
steps.description: The engineer raises a work request in the ERP for each deficiency the area crew can fix (vegetation, riprap, drains, gate seals, instrument repairs) with the priority and target date.

error.defect_description: Request too vague for the crew to plan.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Revise manual or emergency plan
steps.description: The engineer updates the operation, maintenance and surveillance manual or the emergency management plan: contact lists, inundation maps, surveillance frequencies, gate procedures and notification charts, and marks changes for review.

error.defect_description: Out-of-date contact or procedure left in.

control.basis: Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive: OMS manuals and emergency management plans kept current

evidence.note: Manual and plan duties (s1); annual contact review and 7 to 10 year full review in comparable regulation (s8); effort estimated.

steps.name: Share emergency plan and run exercise
steps.description: The engineer sends the updated emergency plan to downstream municipalities and emergency services, and organises a tabletop or notification exercise with them, then records lessons and fixes.

control.basis: Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive: emergency plans shared with stakeholders and tested

evidence.note: Sharing and testing plans (s1); regular exercises with downstream stakeholders (s2); coordination with Calgary and Rocky View County (s4); waits estimated.

steps.name: Scope and procure dam safety review
steps.description: The engineer writes the scope for the periodic dam safety review, gets quotes from qualified engineering firms through supply chain, and issues the service order to the chosen consultant.

evidence.note: Periodic reviews by qualified professionals (s1); 7 to 10 year cycle in comparable regulation (s8); effort estimated.

steps.name: Consultant performs dam safety review
steps.description: The consultant reviews design, construction and performance records, inspects the dam, checks flood and earthquake capacity against current guidelines and writes a draft report with recommendations.

evidence.note: Duration estimated (two to seven months).

steps.name: Review draft dam safety review
steps.description: The engineer checks the draft against the scope and records, challenges recommendations that rest on wrong data, and agrees the final report and the owner's action plan with the consultant.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Draft report or memo
steps.description: The engineer writes the inspection report, annual performance review, instrumentation memo or covering letter, with photos, plots, deficiency table and recommendations, and authenticates it as a professional engineer where it goes to the regulator.

error.defect_description: Inconsistent figures between tables and text.

control.basis: APEGA authentication of engineering documents; Directive requires qualified professionals

evidence.note: Annual performance reviews are a regulatory submission (s9); effort estimated.

steps.name: Area manager reviews report
steps.description: The hydro area manager reads the report for operational effects (reservoir restrictions, gate limits, work that needs outages or budget) and agrees the action dates.

evidence.note: Share of tasks that end in a submission estimated.

steps.name: Director approves submission
steps.description: The director of hydro operations, as the owner's accountable person, reads the summary and signs the covering letter for submissions to the regulator.

control.basis: Owner accountability for dam safety: submissions signed by the accountable director

evidence.note: Owners are accountable for dam safety (s1); approval step estimated.

steps.name: Submit to regulator
steps.description: The engineer uploads the report and covering letter through the provincial submission portal or by email to the dam safety regulator and files the confirmation.

evidence.note: Mandatory compliance reporting (s2, s9).

steps.name: Regulator reviews submission
steps.description: Provincial dam safety staff carry out a technical review of the submission against the Directive and either accept it or send questions and requests for more analysis or work.

evidence.note: Technical review of submissions by the regulator (s2); duration and question rate estimated.

steps.name: Answer regulator questions
steps.description: The engineer prepares answers, extra analysis or a revised report, gets the area manager's agreement on any new commitments and resubmits.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Hazardous condition found
exceptions.description: A finding is reported to the regulator at once, with reservoir restrictions or extra surveillance.

exceptions.name: Dam safety review
exceptions.description: A consultant review takes several months and its recommendations feed the deficiency register.

exceptions.name: Regulator questions
exceptions.description: The regulator asks for more information or work before accepting a submission.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from task opening to filing or regulator acceptance
benchmarks.population: Dam safety tasks at a hydro owner with about 25 regulated structures

evidence.note: Estimate: internal tasks close in about one month; submitted tasks add one to three months of regulator review; dam safety reviews take six months or more. No public benchmark found.

benchmarks.unit: years between dam safety reviews (very high and high consequence dams; 7 for extreme)
benchmarks.population: British Columbia regulated dams, used as a comparable Canadian rule

benchmarks.unit: consequence classes in Alberta (low to extreme)

pain_points.description: Inspections must wait for a season, reservoir level and access window, so a missed window pushes a task by months.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Reports queue behind field work and flood season for a team of four, and wait again for area manager and director review.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Deficiency register and task calendar are kept in spreadsheets, so closing items and proving compliance to the regulator takes manual reconciliation.

evidence.note: Owners must track deficiencies and report them (s1, s2); spreadsheet use estimated.

sources.title: Dam and canal safety regulatory framework
sources.supports: Water (Ministerial) Regulation Part 6 and the Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive; five consequence classes (low, significant, high, very high, extreme) assessed by qualified professionals, accepted by the regulator and reviewed periodically; owners must keep operation, maintenance and surveillance (OMS) manuals and emergency management plans prepared by qualified people, reviewed and tested periodically and shared with key stakeholders; periodic safety assessments by qualified professionals reported to the regulator; owners must track deficiencies and report hazardous conditions and significant changes in operation or surveillance to the Director.

sources.title: Dam and canal safety: regulatory processes
sources.supports: Mandatory compliance reporting by owners on plans, operation, safety assessments and evaluations, with technical review by the regulator; yearly regulator audit inspections scheduled by consequence class; owners document and report deficiencies and the regulator follows up until remediated; owners hold regular emergency exercises with downstream stakeholders.

sources.title: Hydro safety
sources.supports: Water levels near Bearspaw Dam can rise or fall up to 2 metres in a short time; hydro operations support flood control, drought mitigation and irrigation and convey water to licence holders including irrigation districts and municipalities; buffer zones, signs, booms and barriers; regular patrols, inspections, safety audits and infrastructure maintenance; coordination with regulators, police and emergency responders.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Alberta hydro facilities: Bow River system 11 plants (338 MW: Barrier, Bearspaw, Cascade, Ghost, Horseshoe, Interlakes, Kananaskis, Pocaterra, Rundle, Spray, Three Sisters), North Saskatchewan system 2 plants (Bighorn 120 MW, Brazeau 355 MW), Oldman system 4 small plants (21 MW); merchant sale into the Alberta spot market after PPA expiry; value from capacity, energy and ancillary services; Belly River operates April to October.

sources.title: Dam Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 40/2016, Schedule 2
sources.supports: Comparable Canadian regulation used for frequencies: weekly site surveillance for high to extreme dams, annual formal inspection (semi-annual for extreme), annual test operation of spillway gates, outlets and equipment, annual instrumentation analysis, annual review of emergency contacts, OMS manual and emergency plan review every 7 to 10 years, dam safety review every 7 years (extreme) or 10 years (very high, high); prompt notice of hazardous conditions and a written report within 30 days of rectification.

sources.title: Dam safety (AER web page on dams it regulates)
sources.supports: Regulatory submissions reviewed include annual performance reviews, dam safety reviews and emergency management plans under Part 6 of the Water (Ministerial) Regulation and the Alberta Dam and Canal Safety Directive; owners must continuously monitor and assess structural integrity and report dam-related incidents and emergencies; inspection frequency set by consequence classification.

assumptions: Alberta's Dam and Canal Safety Directive text could not be opened (the PDF was not readable), so frequencies of inspections, gate tests, instrument reviews and dam safety reviews are taken from British Columbia's Dam Safety Regulation as a comparable Canadian rule and marked as such.

The process map gives this process no trigger; the workflow treats the provincial requirements (dam_safety_directive) as the calendar trigger and condition reports from maintenance crews (asset_condition_report) as event triggers.
Structure count (about 25 dams, dikes and canals) is an estimate from the 17 plants; several Bow River plants have more than one dam or canal.
Cycle time includes the regulator's review only for the 45 percent of tasks that are submitted; internal tasks end at the area manager's review.
